title: Core App Marketing KPI Analysis
deck: Unify the definitions of CPI/CPA/ARPU/ROAS and judge campaign performance against country/OS/category benchmarks. Absolute numbers without a benchmark are meaningless.
summary: Measure KPIs in 5 layers: (1) efficiency (CPI/CPC), (2) conversion (CPA/CVR), (3) value (ARPU/ARPPU), (4) payback (ROAS), (5) durability (LTV/Retention). Never judge on a single metric — monitor all five together.

content.html: USD basis, Adjust + AppsFlyer aggregate data. Standard deviations across category/country/OS are large — treat as reference only.

items: Step 1: efficiency — confirm CPI/CPC is within ±30% of benchmark. If not, review campaign structure or bidding.
Step 2: quality — within the same campaign, D7 retention should be ≥70% of benchmark. Below that, suspect network traffic quality gaps or a missing deferred deep link.
Step 3: payback — D7 ROAS ≥30% of the break-even LTV/CAC = 1.0 level means learning is on track. At 50%+, bids can go up.
Forbidden pattern: judging campaigns by CPI alone → budget drifts to low-quality-traffic networks. Always co-evaluate with D7 ROAS.

content.title: Network dashboard and Adjust differ by 30%+
content.html: 1) Attribution window mismatch (Meta 1d_click vs Adjust 7d_click). 2) SKAN postback delays land iOS installs on D-2~D-3. 3) Missing cost-data sync. Use Adjust numbers as the SSOT for all analysis.

content.title: ARPU is good but ROAS is bad
content.html: You're catching high-value users but acquisition is too expensive. 1) Lower bids −10%. 2) Try the same LTV group on cheaper networks. 3) Narrow the Lookalike seed for tighter targeting.
